note: Simulated review by an AI model (Journal-Fit Reviewer / EIC integration call); role-separated, not independent. RESPONSE.md treated as untrusted author persuasion. No letter pointer located manuscript evidence meeting a Phase-1 operationalization beyond what 2A recorded, no rebuttal was offered, and no scope misreading was revealed, so no adjustment is booked and every final verdict equals its 2A verdict. The new-issue set (NEW-10..NEW-12) stays frozen in phase2a_verdicts.json and is not restated here.

rows.authors_claim: Uniform independent starts now attributed to the original models (deffuant2000, hegselmann2002).
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Accurate. text: Sec.3 para 1, 'For opinions drawn independently and uniformly, as in the original BC models' with both citations; no prevalence claim remains.
Letter lists R2 under 'Still open ... Deferred by the author'; accurate. text: Code and data, '[Zenodo DOI to be added]' unchanged. The letter makes no claim about the Appendix B parameter gaps.
rows.residual_gap: Element (ii) unmet: the DOI is still printed as '[Zenodo DOI to be added]' and refs.bib still says 'DOI to be added on archiving' (an author deferral leaves (ii) unmet). Element (i) still incomplete: Appendix B does not give the case's shared epsilon or the start/run-matched cosine thresholds, the influence-weight function (only 'grows with its degree'), the per-dimension bias weights (only 'a fixed per-dimension weight'), whether trust is static, or the general perception formula for a non-origin trust target. Elements (iii)-(v) and the draft-engine commit 50a42e5 are retained. No made-worse trigger.

rows.authors_claim: New appendix table of five secondary outcomes under all four rules per geometry; paragraph justifies 'recommended' design; start-matched +0.032 against run-matched +0.034.
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Accurate as far as it goes. table: tab:secondary has the five outcomes x four rules x two geometries; text: Sec.5.2 'Which target', 'removes both of the draft's couplings' and '(+0.032 against +0.034)'. The letter is silent on element (c): text: Sec.4.1 'a window that ends before most opinion groups have formed' is unchanged.
rows.residual_gap: (c) unmet: Sec.4.1 still asserts that the first 100 rounds form 'a window that ends before most opinion groups have formed' with no supporting numbers (e.g. share of eventual groups formed by round 100), and it is not removed or qualified. (a) and (b) are met; on (b) the justification explains the centred gate and anchor pull and calls run-matching 'our choice of estimand' backed by a near-identical start-matched interaction, which is accepted, though 'couplings' is not defined elsewhere.

rows.authors_claim: Fortunato described as comparing confidence-region shapes; Huet and Kurahashi described by what they show, paragraph says how they bear on this note; checked against abstracts.
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Partly accurate. text: Sec.2 para 1, the Fortunato sentence matches its abstract and Kurahashi has a tying sentence; but Huet gets no tie beyond 'These studies show that the shape of the confidence region matters', which contradicts the Fortunato finding just reported. Overstated (see letter_overstatements).
rows.residual_gap: (a) is met for the Fortunato sentence itself, which matches its abstract (external: https://arxiv.org/abs/physics/0504017: thresholds coincide with or are very close to their one-dimensional counterparts). (b) is unmet for Schweighofer 2020 and Baumann 2021, which are still named only in a list clause, and Huet 2008 gets a description but no statement of how the note relates to it beyond the collective sentence. Also, the new collective sentence 'These studies show that the shape of the confidence region matters' contradicts Fortunato's finding as the previous sentence reports it (thresholds close to the 1-D ones, i.e. shape mattered little). This is a peripheral mis-description; it should be qualified.

rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Accurate. text: Sec.6 box item 4, 'Check for monotone equivalence (a known identity, stated here as a lemma)'.

rows.authors_claim: Radial spread and directional dispersion defined; run-matched radial gap reported (1.48, 1.49), going in both directions (22 cells positive, 14 negative).

The '22 positive, 14 negative' counts appear nowhere in the manuscript (no per-cell radial table) and pool 36 cases. Overstated (see letter_overstatements).

rows.authors_claim: The 4 calibrations not equivalent on evaluation seeds are flagged in the table; audit item 3 gives pilot-size guidance.
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Accurate. table: tab:calibration, four rows carry the dagger; text: Sec.6 box item 3, 'use enough pilot seeds that the standard error of the pilot pass rate is below the tolerance'. The letter does not claim the +-0.005 boundary cells are flagged; they are not.
rows.residual_gap: (b) is met. (a) is only partly met: the four non-equivalent cases are flagged, but the five cells at exactly +-0.005 pilot error (centred d=2 c=.15 cosine, centred d=2 c=.30 angular, centred d=4 c=.30 angular, centred d=8 c=.05 cosine, unit d=8 c=.30 angular) and the many cells whose evaluation gap exceeds the 0.005 tolerance (e.g. -0.025, +0.013, -0.009, +0.008) are still unmarked, so they can be found only by reading the columns.

rows.authors_claim: Every headline summary in abstract and Sec.4 split by geometry out of 18; 'one gate' and 'common ruler' now equivalence results (18/18, 18/18, own ruler 10/18); new tab:cos-ang.
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Mostly accurate: text: Abstract, 'equivalent in 10 of 18 ... equivalent in 18 of 18'; text: Sec.4.2, 'equivalent in pass rate in 18 of 18 cells'; table: tab:cos-ang exists. But text: Sec.4.1, 'the pass-rate gap is equivalent to zero in 32 of 36 cases' remains pooled (32 = 16 + 16), so 'every headline summary ... separately' is overstated. The letter is silent on residual elements (i) secondary-outcome CIs and (ii) case-margin timing ('a margin fixed before this analysis', Sec.5.2, unchanged).
rows.residual_gap: (i) unmet: per-cell CIs are still printed only for the pass rate, the primary outcome and the cosine-angular comparison; the secondary outcomes (variance, radial spread, directional dispersion, effective groups, convergence time) appear only as medians with equivalence counts and no CIs. (ii) unmet: the case margin is still described as 'a margin fixed before this analysis', with no disclosure that it was set after the round-2 own-target interval it tests had been reported. (iv) mostly met, but one pooled count remains: Sec.4.1 gives 'equivalent to zero in 32 of 36 cases' (cosine+angular pooled, the same run-matched pass-rate gaps reported separately as 16 and 16). (iii) met for 'one gate'/'common ruler'/own-target 'disappears'; (v) met. Peripheral made-worse trigger carried here: the new 'the start-matched version gives almost the same interaction (+0.032 against +0.034)' is a no-difference claim added without an equivalence test. It is not on the core and does not outweigh the progress, so PARTIALLY_ADDRESSED under the precedence rule.

rows.authors_claim: gestefeld2023 (trust in government, calibrated to survey data) cited as a possible source of evidence on the trust target; checked against the JASSS page.
rows.claim_vs_manuscript: Accurate. text: Sec.2 'Alignment and policy models', 'trust in government is itself modelled and calibrated to survey data by gestefeld2023, which suggests where evidence on the target could come from'. No policy or regulatory ABM with trust-scaled signals is claimed or added.
rows.residual_gap: Institutional-trust modelling is now cited, and accurately: the paper calibrates to ESS institutional-trust items and SHP trust in government (external: https://www.jasss.org/26/4/9.html). But no policy or regulatory ABM that uses trust or credibility scaling of a signal is cited. The trust-target/origin audit is not positioned against how such models scale signals by trust. Gestefeld & Lorenz model trust as an opinion, not as a multiplier, and the text does not draw that contrast.

letter_claims_counting_note: 27 checkable claims: 5 R13 bullets, 20 table rows (including the '18cells' spacing fix, confirmed: no number-then-'cells' run remains in revised/main.tex) and 2 'Still open' lines. 24 are accurate and 3 overstated. Accurate claims that leave residuals unmentioned (R3(c), R13(i)-(ii), the S1 crossing-run row, NEW-3 ODD, NEW-6 isolation, the NEW-7 100-round claim) count as accurate: silence is not overstatement.
post_letter_observations: C5: the letter says C5 is 'not pursued', but roadmap.json records author_triage will_address for C5. The triage record and the letter disagree; next round should take the triage from the author-adjudication sidecar and ask the author to reconcile the two.

NEW-4: the letter's check that Euclidean unit cells are settled at least as often as their centred twins holds in Table tab:settled (all 9 pairs), but it is letter-side only. Stating it in Sec.5 with the size of the gap (e.g. d=2, c=0.05: 60%/22% unit against 66%/31% centred) would be a first step toward the 'quantified' half of the NEW-4 criterion.
R11/S1: if the radial direction counts are added to the manuscript, they should be split by geometry (out of 18 each), consistent with the R13 split, not the letter's pooled 22/14 of 36.

S4: the letter's 'positive in all 36 cases' is another pooled count. The manuscript's wording ('in every cell for both geometries', run-matched) is correctly scoped; Table tab:secondary shows a negative shared-rule cosine signed variance median (-0.55), so the claim must stay scoped to run-matching.

R13: the letter's 'Both tests use the paper's existing margins (+-0.02 pass rate, +-0.25 log2), fixed before analysis' is accurate for the minimal model (Sec.4.1, 'fixed before the runs of this version were analysed') but says nothing about the case-study margin +-0.01 in Sec.5.2, where the residual (ii) disclosure is still owed.

The letter is headed 'in progress' and says unlisted items are still open, yet it lists R3, R13, S1, NEW-3, NEW-6 and NEW-7 as changed without noting their open criterion elements. The next letter should say per item which elements remain open.
